# #676 — [cutover-note] DB_NAME silently defaults to open_brain — identity-selecting config with a fallback (ledger 28/31)

State: OPEN

Found by the pre-cutover config audit (2026-08-09). Identity-config-loud-on-absence review (ledger 28/31).

## The one that matters
src/db/pool.ts:22 — DB_NAME defaults to \`open_brain\` if unset. This SELECTS WHICH BRAIN you connect to: a core01 deploy missing DB_NAME from its env connects to a database named open_brain and, if one exists, silently serves it. Same class as the capture-health namespace ruling (identity-selecting), but with a silent fallback instead of a loud refusal. On a cutover this is how you serve the wrong database and not know.

## Lesser, same family
- OPEN_BRAIN_SERVER_IP / OPEN_BRAIN_BIND_HOST unset → LAN detection then literal "unknown" (CONFIG_REFERENCE.md:151-166): /health advertises a guessed identity. Bounded to private ranges; low severity but a guess presented as fact.
- OPEN_BRAIN_RUN_MIGRATIONS defaults ON (src/index.ts:320, !== "0") — fail-open for schema mutation; interacts with the unversioned-plist blocker (#675 B2): if the plist omits it for a non-primary worker, both workers migrate.
- SERVICE_NAME / OPEN_BRAIN_WORKER_NAME default/unset — log attribution only, note.

## Also
docs/CONFIG_REFERENCE.md self-admits it was measured against src/ on 2026-07-30, predates server/, and documents none of the capture-health keys. Worth a refresh pass so the cutover has an accurate config map.

## Wanted (operator ruling per ledger 28/31 — required config, loud on absence)
Make DB_NAME required-no-fallback at minimum; decide the rest. Then a done-means check that a missing identity key fails loudly rather than defaulting. Not a lane's call to change identity-config semantics silently.
